newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian Rouble slips on increased money supply.
newsitem.headline: Russian Rouble slips on increased money supply.

text.p: The rouble slipped on Wednesday and is under pressure because of recent increases in the money supply by the central bank, dealers said.
rouble/dollar Feb 12 midday Feb 12 early Feb 11 close
"We have been seeing a steady growth in money supply, controlled by the central bank, for the last month and a half," said Alexander Suchkov, chief dealer at United Investment Bank.
He said the main factor behind money supply growth was treasury tax exemptions -- paper issued by the Finance Ministry to pay the governments' debts and accepted by the government in lieu of taxes.
The Finance Ministry stopped issuing the exemptions some time ago on the insistence of the International Monetary Fund, but Suchkov said they were having a delayed effect.
He also said growing foreign investment in government securities and shares, converted into roubles, was also increasing rouble money supply.
Neftekhimbank dealer Vladimir Zrazhevsky forecast the rouble would weaken as banks withdraw funds from government securities, where yields were falling.
